title: Annual winter density reduces oxygen model errors at BATS and on western North Atlantic sections, but not on A05
abstract: A North Atlantic ventilation model driven by decade-mean winter fields missed large oxygen changes on sigma0 26.5. We test a correction from annual winter density at a one-year lag. The model parameters stay fixed. At BATS, five-year blocked tests with two-year gaps reduce annual AOU error from 5.86 to 3.50 umol/kg. A fit through 2003 reduces 2004-2025 error from 6.17 to 4.39. Neither annual density alone nor the decade-forced model works as well as their combination. A BATS-only coefficient reduces error of six A20/A22 section changes from 11.58 to 3.13; the early-fit coefficient gives 6.98. A05 error rises from 0.37 to 7.21. These results support a missing fast winter response in the western record, but not a basin-wide correction. The section test was added after the BATS result. The fit is statistical and cannot separate ventilation from oxygen use. The short record, shared climate history and unstable slope limit attribution and projections.
